name: Liraglutide
summary: A once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist used for type 2 diabetes and obesity that lowers glucose and weight with a demonstrated cardiovascular benefit.
mechanism: Activates the GLP-1 receptor, increasing glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppressing glucagon, slowing gastric emptying, and reducing appetite.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers A1c and body weight; reduces major adverse cardiovascular events in high-risk type 2 diabetes (LEADER).

pharmacokinetics.elimination: Proteolytic degradation; no single organ of elimination

dosing.adult: Diabetes: 0.6 mg SC daily for 1 week, then 1.2 mg daily, may increase to 1.8 mg; obesity (Saxenda): titrate to 3.0 mg daily

contraindications: Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma
warnings: Nausea and GI intolerance, especially during titration
Renal function can worsen with dehydration from GI losses
safety.overdose: Severe nausea, vomiting; supportive care. Hypoglycemia unlikely alone

indications: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, with cardiovascular risk reduction in high-risk patients
Obesity or overweight with comorbidities (Saxenda 3.0 mg)
clinicalPearls: Titration is tolerability engineering — escalate weekly per label to limit nausea.
Daily injection distinguishes it from weekly GLP-1s; the 3.0 mg dose is the weight-management regimen.
good: Daily GLP-1 with CV benefit and meaningful weight loss; flexible dosing.
bad: Significant GI intolerance, history of pancreatitis, or personal/family history of MTC.
